text:
When someone received compensation through the miscarriage of justice compensation scheme, this was classed as capital when working out means-tested benefits. This sometimes meant they would not be eligible for means-tested benefits.

A means-tested benefit means your income and capital will usually be taken into account when calculating your eligibility.

From 22 July 2025, the Department for Work and Pensions is no longer counting this compensation as capital and income when calculating means-tested benefits in Great Britain. The same rules apply to people living in Northern Ireland.

The United Kingdom Government and Devolved Governments compensation schemes for miscarriages of justice gives compensation when someone has been convicted of a criminal offence and:

their conviction has been reversed

a new or newly discovered fact shows beyond reasonable doubt that there has been a miscarriage of justice

1. Who may be affected

If you have received a compensation payment for a miscarriage of justice, you might be affected if you:

currently claim means-tested benefits

could not claim means-tested benefits because you had too much capital or income

2. What to do next

If you are affected, what you do next will depend on:

if you currently claim means-tested benefits

if you do not currently claim means-tested benefits

2.1 If you currently claim means-tested benefits

From 22 July 2025, you need to report a change of circumstances if you claim:

Universal Credit

Pension Credit

Housing Benefit

income-based Jobseeker’s Allowance

income-related Employment and Support Allowance

Income Support

Your change of circumstances should explain you’ve previously received compensation through the miscarriage of justice compensation scheme, and that this is no longer classed as capital.

The department will be able to consider your benefits to ensure you are receiving the correct amount. You will need to provide a copy of your compensation award notification.

2.2 If you do not currently claim means-tested benefits

From 22 July 2025, check your eligibility for:

Universal Credit

Pension Credit

Housing Benefit

Any compensation payments you received will not be taken into account as capital when calculating entitlement to these benefits.

You will need to provide a copy of your compensation award as part of the application process.
